subject: Orchestrated app sprint & credential runbook
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@lakesidehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Orchestrated app sprint & credential runbook

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As discussed, Lakeside is planning to onboard three additional internal apps (Patient Intake UI, Claims Processor, and Analytics ETL) over the next 6–8 weeks. To keep the pilot stable while enabling scale, I put together a short runbook and credential request template to drive the rollout. Please see attached and the brief plan below: 

High-level plan (proposal)
- Week 0: kickoff + finalize projects and point people
- Week 1: issue API keys + run a developer sandbox smoke test (prefill traffic)
- Week 2–3: canary routing for 1 app (10% traffic) + telemetry checks
- Week 4–6: staggered activation for other apps + capacity increase commit

Immediate asks for you:
1) Confirm the three app owners and their technical leads
2) Share any preferred key naming convention or tagging policy
3) Estimated daily requests per app for baseline capacity planning

Attachments included: runbook_v1.pdf, key_request_template.xlsx, canary_matrix.csv

I’m looping Ben (AM) on commercial items and Marissa (CS) on rollout support. Happy to run a brief 30-min kickoff next week — are you available Tue/Wed morning (PT)?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0128

From: Jordan Park <jordan.park@lakesidehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Li <ava.li@lakesidehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchestrated app sprint & credential runbook

Laura —

Thanks for this and the clear runbook. A few clarifications from our side: 

- App owners: Patient Intake (Ava Li), Claims Processor (Michael Cheng), Analytics ETL (Ravi Patel) — I cc'd Ava to confirm.
- Key policy: We prefer project-prefixed keys (e.g., lakeside.patientintake.prod) and per-environment tags. Full policy attached in our internal ticket (I gave you access).
- Traffic: rough estimates — Intake: 120k req/day, Claims: 40k req/day, ETL: 8k req/day (burst 50k during month-end).

On the timeline: Tue/Wed mornings next week work for a kickoff — Tue 10/3 9:30am PT preferred.

Two procurement items: 1) we need an updated SOW with the phased activation schedule; 2) procurement will require an amendment listing the additional API key buckets and expected monthly units before we sign the PO. I’ll loop procurement separately.

Jordan Park
Director, Platform Ops | Lakeside Health
jordan.park@lakesidehealth.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orchestrated app sprint & credential runbook — kickoff confirmed + MAP

Jordan / Ava —

Great — Tue 11/3 9:30am PT (I think Jordan meant 11/3, earlier typo) works for our team. I updated the runbook with a lightweight Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and attached the templates you can drop into your change control. Key highlights in the MAP: 

Mutual Action Plan (summary)
- Kickoff (11/03): attendees = Platform Ops, 1x Eng lead per app, Redwood CS, Redwood AM
- Keys issued (target 11/04): dev keys + 3 prod keys per app (named per lakeside policy)
- Canary (11/10–11/16): route 10% user traffic for Patient Intake only; monitoring window = 72 hours for SLO checks
- Capacity commit (11/17): Redwood to provision an intermediate capacity bump for Claims (to handle 50k/day bursts) — commercial to finalize commit levels
- Contract amendment (by 11/13): updated SOW listing per-app expected monthly units for procurement

I attached: runbook_v1.pdf (MAP included), key_request_template.xlsx (please fill owner, environment, requested TTL), canary_matrix.csv (metrics to monitor).

Ben — can you validate the proposed capacity bump and provide a short note on pricing impact? Marissa — CS will lead smoke-test checklists and can host the post-canary retro.

Thanks — see you Tue.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Orchestrated app sprint & credential runbook — support plan and checklist

Jordan / Ava —

Looking forward to the kickoff. A couple quick notes from CS so the canary window behaves as expected: 
- We’ll provision a staging sandbox identical to prod for keys/test tokens by 11/04
- Smoke checklist (high level): auth/latency, token rotation, KV cache warmup, sampling traces to Redwood Console
- Post-canary retro (11/17): 30 min call to confirm health metrics and go/no-go for the next app

Also attaching a light ops playbook we use for canaries (I pasted the most important checks into the runbook). If you want, I can run the first smoke test with Ava and her engineer on 11/05.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Procurement <procurement@lakesidehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Lakeside — Amendment request for additional API key buckets

Hi Laura / Ben —

Procurement here. We reviewed the MAP and can proceed, but need an amendment to the existing contract that: 
1) Lists the three additional API key buckets and environments (dev/stage/prod)
2) States expected monthly units per bucket (we will use your MAP estimates as placeholders if you provide them)
3) Notes the timeline for activation (canary and phased activation dates)

Please send a redline or updated SOW by COB Friday 11/13 so we can attach it to the PO. Also include a point estimate for the Claims capacity bump (expected monthly units) so we can budget.

Thanks,
Lakeside Procurement
procurement@lakesidehealth.com
